clue.text: Renegade taking new track, coming back with cover

indicators.note: something coming back travels the opposite way, so the word for the path is read right to left

blocks.note: a rut is a track worn by wheels
N is the standard abbreviation for new
a coat covers, as a coat of paint does

explanation.surface: A deserter heads off down a fresh path, then doubles back wearing a disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed track comes first, then new, then the cover: TUR + N + COAT gives TURNCOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who switches sides, which is exactly what a renegade does.

clue.text: Complete novel hot and unrefined

indicators.note: novel means new, so the word after it takes a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
rough means crude or unpolished

explanation.surface: A book that is steamy and crude through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorough means done in full with nothing left out, as in a complete or utter search.

clue.text: Coin in bank not long ago

indicators.note: in tells us the money word is placed inside the other word

blocks.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: Money was paid into an account a short while back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently describes something happening a short time before now.

clue.text: Pen exclusive story, opening out

indicators.note: with the opening out, the first letter of the story word is dropped

blocks.note: a scoop is a news story one paper has before its rivals

explanation.surface: A journalist writes an exclusive that begins by revealing all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a verb about writing but it is a noun for an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop is an enclosure for keeping poultry, the same idea as a pen for livestock.

clue.text: Stupendous ace, with energy in victory, bound to enthral one

indicators.note: in tells us the energy letter goes inside the word for victory
to enthral is to hold captive, so the bound word holds the numeral inside it

blocks.note: A is ace on playing cards
a win is a victory
E is the symbol for energy
a bound is a leap or spring
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A star player storms to victory and is certain to captivate everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: A + W(E)IN + SP(I)RING. 'Bound' here is a leap, not 'certain'.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe-inspiring and stupendous both describe something so impressive it astonishes onlookers.

clue.text: Servile, yielding fine shelter

indicators.note: yielding here means giving up, so the servile word surrenders the letter for fine

blocks.note: fawning means grovelling and obsequious
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A meek, submissive person gives up a perfectly good place to shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: FAWNING without its F leaves AWNING.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas canopy fixed over a window or shopfront to keep off sun and rain.

clue.text: Antelope stew edible after preparation

indicators.note: food after preparation has been chopped and mixed, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Game meat cooked in a casserole becomes good to eat once prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest, or gnu, is a large African antelope known for its mass migrations.

clue.text: Silliness, freezing outside studio? Not half

indicators.note: not half means only half is kept, so the first half of the workplace word goes
outside says the cold word wraps round the remaining letters

blocks.note: icy means freezing cold
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a chilly artist's workroom is really that foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps the back half of the workplace word, and the question mark flags that a studio is not really being called silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiocy is foolish behaviour or extreme stupidity, a stronger form of silliness.

clue.text: Musical nation by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase says we want a word that is heard, not spelt, like the country

blocks.note: the country in south-east Europe

explanation.surface: A country said to be a musical one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' reads as an adjective describing the nation, but it is a noun: a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is the 1970s stage musical, later a film with John Travolta and Olivia Newton-John.

clue.text: Quick examination previously done

blocks.note: once means at some earlier time
over means finished, as in the game is over

explanation.surface: A brief inspection that was carried out some time back.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving something the once-over means looking it over rapidly and superficially, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Fish situation reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that is heard the same way

blocks.note: a situation is a location or site

explanation.surface: A news item on where some fish has been found.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flatfish with orange spots, common in British fish shops.

clue.text: When caught by reckless foul, landed abruptly

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it, so the small word goes within
reckless suggests wild and careless, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: as means when, as in as I left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer, hacked down by a wild tackle, hits the ground hard.
explanation.definitionFit: All of a sudden is an idiom meaning unexpectedly and without warning, the same as abruptly.

clue.text: Grunting sound from buffalo in Kansas

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the animal and the start of the state

explanation.surface: A noise made by a bison out on the Kansas plains.
explanation.walkthrough: A buffalo grunts, but the sound wanted is a pig's; it sits across buffalO IN Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the conventional representation of the grunt a pig makes.

clue.text: Leads nun's life, organised around church

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so those letters get rearranged
around says the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun's daily routine, built around her church, guides her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads' looks like a plural noun but is a verb: someone leads or influences others.
explanation.definitionFit: To influence people is to sway or guide them, which is one sense of leading them.

clue.text: Destroyed enormous area over time in action

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so what precedes it comes first
in tells us the preceding letters are placed inside the action word

blocks.note: a deed is an act or action
vast means huge
A is the abbreviation for area
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A huge region laid waste over time during fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the size-and-area pair above the time letter, and that trio then sits inside the action word.
explanation.definitionFit: Devastated means laid waste or ruined completely, as destroyed means.

clue.text: Bird journal reflected study by quiet enthusiast

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror flips left and right, so that word reads backwards

blocks.note: a log is a daily record or journal
a den is a private study room
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a lover of something is a fan of it

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sits in a quiet study pondering their diary of sightings.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden plover is a wading bird with gold-spangled plumage, found on moors and fields.

clue.text: Gear I changed after damage in match

indicators.note: changed means altered, so those letters are put into a different order
after puts the rearranged letters behind the damage word

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A racing team swaps its kit after a crash during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a sporting contest, but here it means a union of two people.
explanation.definitionFit: A match can mean a pairing in wedlock, as in a good match, which is a marriage.

clue.text: Unerring in following criminal

blocks.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
lawless means breaking the law

explanation.surface: Perfect at tailing a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawless means without any fault or mistake, just as unerring means never going wrong.

clue.text: Fortification held in wars ruined entirely

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the two little words are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: held and had both mean possessed
taken as written
all means wholly, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A stronghold that survived wars is now completely in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian's Wall is the Roman defensive barrier built across northern England in the second century.

clue.text: Play, not hard, imbued with universal charm

indicators.note: not tells us the following letter is left out of the play
imbued with means filled with, so the shortened play takes a letter inside

blocks.note: Hamlet is Shakespeare's tragedy
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
U is the film rating for universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: A light-hearted drama with broad appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' suggests fun, but it is Shakespeare's tragedy; U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn as protection against evil, a lucky trinket.

clue.text: Contract for example including name and length of life

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the abbreviation takes a letter inside

blocks.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
N is the abbreviation for name
a person's age is how long they have lived

explanation.surface: A sample contract that names the parties and its duration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun but is the verb: to hire.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone is to contract or hire them for work.

clue.text: Not entertained by low wit lacking variety

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so the first word goes inside the next

blocks.note: to low is to make the sound a cow makes
taken as written
nous is common sense or intelligence

explanation.surface: Someone unamused by a dull joke that is always the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the verb for a cow's call, not 'deep' or 'sad'; nous is British slang for practical wits.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotonous describes something tediously unchanging, the same tone or pattern over and over.

clue.text: Develop good argument

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: Building up a strong case in a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow is to increase or mature, just as something develops over time.

clue.text: Very happy making broth?

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
up means cheerful, as in feeling up

explanation.surface: Someone delighted to be cooking a pot of broth.
explanation.definitionFit: Broth is a thin, liquid dish made by simmering meat or vegetables in water.

clue.text: Sign about insect in outhouse

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the star sign wraps round the small creature

blocks.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A notice put up about bugs found in the shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' suggests a notice, but it is a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall, a kind of outbuilding.

clue.text: Commercial poll containing account about support

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the poll word takes in what follows
about means turned round, so that short abbreviation is read backwards

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial on TV
a poll is a vote
AC is an abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A TV advert for an opinion poll, with a story about funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' is the verb here: to back a cause publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a cause is to speak up for it and back it publicly.

clue.text: In conclusion, consumed by effort

indicators.note: what is consumed by something ends up inside it, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
the end is the conclusion

explanation.surface: Finally, someone is worn out by hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition, but it means fashionable, as in the in thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in is currently fashionable, and trendy is the informal word for that.

clue.text: Revolutionary move secures extracts

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the next two words are read backwards

blocks.note: to step is to move a foot
pins fastens or holds in place

explanation.surface: A political radical's manoeuvre locks down some pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: STEP + PINS gives STEPPINS, which backwards reads SNIPPETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Snippets are small pieces cut or quoted from something longer, the same as extracts.
